title: What AI Does—and Does Not Do
summary: Build a beginner mental model of generative AI by separating the model from the application, retrieval, tools, and agentic workflow, then verify generated answers against supplied evidence.
objectives: Distinguish a model, an AI-enabled application, retrieval, a tool, and an agentic workflow.
Identify which supplied evidence supports each factual statement in a generated answer.
Correct a fluent answer that conflicts with its source material without guessing why the model produced the error.
Recognize that useful generative capabilities do not guarantee factual accuracy.
Explain when a person should verify, narrow, or stop an AI-assisted task.

sections.title: Define the parts before judging the answer
paragraphs: A model is a mathematical construct that processes input data and returns output. In a language model, the input and output are represented as tokens. A token is an atomic unit such as a word, character, or part of a word. During inference, a trained language model generates a response to an input prompt. A prompt is text supplied to condition the model's behavior. These definitions come from the Google Machine Learning Glossary listed in Sources.

A context window is the number of tokens a model can process in a prompt. It is finite. Supplying a fact in the prompt or retrieved context can help the model use that fact, but it does not guarantee that every generated statement will match the fact.

An application is the larger product or program through which a person uses a model. An application can place a user interface, files, search, memory, policies, tools, and deterministic code around a model. The model is one component of that application, not the whole application.

Retrieval is the step that locates stored material, such as notes or documents, and supplies selected material for use. The retrieved note remains the source of its facts. The model can summarize or transform the note, but the model does not become the source.

For this lesson, a tool means a callable software function that performs a defined operation outside the language model, such as calculating the number of days between two dates. This is an operational definition used to describe the fictional systems below. It is not a claim that every AI application has this feature.

An agent is software that can reason about user input to plan and execute actions on the user's behalf. An agentic workflow can combine state, tools, feedback, and model-directed continuation. A model may propose the next action, while the surrounding application controls which actions are permitted and records their results.
sections.callout: Keep five labels separate: model generates an output, application connects the parts, retrieval locates stored material, a tool performs a defined operation, and an agentic workflow chooses and sequences permitted actions.

sections.title: Useful generation is not automatic evidence
paragraphs: Generative systems can perform tasks such as explaining, summarizing, transforming, classifying, extracting, comparing, brainstorming, translating, drafting, writing code, and analyzing supplied data. A multimodal model accepts or produces more than one modality, such as both images and text. These capabilities are task categories, not promises that every application supports every input or performs every task correctly.

Generated statements can be fabricated, stale, overly broad, biased, internally inconsistent, or unsupported by the supplied material. The Google Machine Learning Glossary calls plausible-seeming but factually incorrect output about the real world a hallucination. In this lesson, use the broader and more observable phrase unsupported or conflicting statement whenever the evidence is enough to identify the mismatch but not enough to establish its internal cause.

Do not infer why a model produced a particular sentence. A visible conflict can establish that an answer is wrong relative to a source, but it does not reveal whether the cause involved retrieval ranking, prompt interpretation, model generation, application code, or another system detail. Report the observable mismatch and correct it from evidence.

Models do not automatically know private records, current events, local policies, or a user's unstated intent. An application may provide some of that information through a prompt, retrieval, files, or tools. Verification must therefore ask both whether the system received relevant evidence and whether the final answer accurately reflects it.
sections.callout: Fluent wording is an output characteristic. It is not independent evidence that a factual statement is correct.

sections.title: Fictional application and stated assumptions
paragraphs: The worked example uses a fictional application named Community Desk Assistant. It is not a description of a real product. For the scenario only, assume the application contains a language model, a retrieval index of staff notes, and a date-difference tool. It also contains an agentic workflow that may retrieve notes, call the date tool, ask the model for a draft, and present that draft to a person.

Assume retrieval returns the two notes shown in the worked example exactly as written. Assume the date-difference tool accepts date-only inputs in the same timezone and calendar context. It counts midnight-to-midnight date transitions from the first date to the second date and excludes the starting date. Under this convention, 2026-10-05 through 2026-10-10 crosses 5 transitions, even though counting both included calendar-date labels would produce 6 dates. The tool therefore returns 5 elapsed whole days. Assume the workflow cannot send or publish a message. A person must inspect and approve the draft.

These capabilities are scenario assumptions supplied for learning. They are not evidence that any named commercial system has retrieval, tools, memory, autonomous action, or the same behavior. No paid account, software setup, or code is needed. Read the supplied text and compare it directly.

sections.title: Worked example: request, source notes, and candidate answer
paragraphs: Fictional scenario date: Monday, October 5, 2026. A community-center employee asks Community Desk Assistant to prepare a reminder. All required inputs appear below.

Actual request: "Using the two staff notes below, write exactly two sentences reminding pottery students about pickup. Use the most recent note for event details. Include the full pickup date, time, room, and the number of elapsed whole days from October 5, 2026 to pickup. Do not add details that the notes do not support."
Source note A, updated September 30, 2026: "Pottery pickup is Saturday, October 10, 2026, from 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. in Room B. This update replaces the September 15 note."
Source note B, dated September 15, 2026: "Pottery pickup is Saturday, October 10, 2026, from 9:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. in Room A."

Supplied tool result: "Elapsed whole days from 2026-10-05 to 2026-10-10: 5." Under the scenario convention, this means 5 midnight-to-midnight transitions, with October 5 excluded as the starting date. It is not an inclusive count of the 6 calendar-date labels October 5 through October 10.
Candidate answer: "Pottery pickup is Saturday, October 10, 2026, from 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. in Room A. Pickup is 5 days after October 5, 2026."

The candidate contains one detectable factual mistake. Do not invent another input, search the web, or guess about the model's training. Every fact needed to find and correct the mistake is supplied here.

sections.title: Worked example: decide from evidence step by step
paragraphs: Decision 1, identify the requested output. The employee requested exactly two sentences containing the pickup date, time, room, and elapsed-day count. This is a bounded drafting task because both the content requirements and the available evidence are explicit.

Decision 2, select the governing source. Note A is dated September 30, 2026, while note B is dated September 15, 2026. Note A is therefore more recent. It also explicitly states that it replaces the September 15 note. The date and replacement sentence both support using note A for the event details.

Decision 3, check each claim rather than judging the paragraph by its fluency. The candidate's date, October 10, matches note A. Its time, 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m., matches note A. Its elapsed-day count, 5, matches the supplied tool result and the scenario convention: date-only inputs in the same timezone and calendar context cross 5 midnight-to-midnight transitions from October 5 to October 10 because the starting date is excluded. Counting both endpoints as calendar-date labels would give 6 labels, but that is not the tool's elapsed-day rule. Its room, Room A, conflicts with note A, which says Room B.

Decision 4, describe only what the evidence establishes. The detectable mistake is the room. The evidence does not establish why that text appeared. It would be unwarranted to claim that the model relied on training data, ignored retrieval, copied the older note for a particular internal reason, or lacked access to a tool.

Decision 5, correct the conflicting claim while preserving supported claims and the requested two-sentence format. Demonstrated corrected answer: "Pottery pickup is Saturday, October 10, 2026, from 10:00 a.m. to 12:00 p.m. in Room B. Pickup is 5 days after October 5, 2026."

Decision 6, connect the parts of the fictional system. The application receives the prompt and coordinates the other components. Retrieval locates notes A and B. The date tool supplies the value 5. The model drafts the two sentences from the supplied context. The agentic workflow sequences retrieval, the tool call, and drafting, then stops for human review because the fictional system is not permitted to publish.

Decision 7, preserve the evidence boundary. Note A is the source for the event date, time, and room. The supplied tool result is the source for the elapsed-day count. Retrieval is how the notes were located. The model is the drafting component, not the authority for either the event details or the calculation.
sections.callout: A precise correction has three parts: name the conflicting claim, cite the supplied evidence that contradicts it, and replace only what the evidence supports replacing.

sections.title: Worked example: component map and verification result
paragraphs: Model: generates the requested reminder using the prompt and supplied context. The model can transform evidence into concise prose, but its draft still requires checking.
Application: provides the interface, sends selected context to the model, exposes the date tool, enforces the no-publishing permission, and displays the draft for review.

Retrieval: locates both staff notes. It does not decide by itself which sentence is correct, and it does not make either note true. The note text and its update relationship are the evidence to inspect.

Tool: calculates the elapsed whole-day difference under the scenario's stated rule for date-only inputs in the same timezone and calendar context. It counts midnight-to-midnight transitions and excludes the starting date, so October 5 to October 10 is 5 transitions rather than an inclusive count of 6 calendar-date labels. Its supplied result is 5. A tool result can also require verification in real work, but no extra calculation is required for this activity because the result is an explicit input.

Agentic workflow: chooses and sequences permitted steps. In this fictional case, it retrieves, calls the date tool, requests a draft, and pauses for approval. An agent is not merely a long answer. The planning and execution of actions are what make the workflow agentic.

Verification result: revise Room A to Room B, keep the supported date, time, and count, and approve only the corrected answer. This conclusion uses no numerical risk score and makes no unsupported claim about hidden model behavior.

sections.title: Learner variation: library reminder inputs
paragraphs: This is a second fictional scenario. Scenario date: Tuesday, November 3, 2026. The fictional application is Library Message Helper. For this exercise, assume it has the same component pattern as the earlier fictional application: a language model, retrieval over the two supplied notices, a date-difference tool, and an agentic workflow that must stop for staff approval.

Actual request: "Using the two library notices below, write exactly two sentences reminding members about the robotics club. Use the most recent notice for meeting details. Include the full meeting date, time, room, the number of elapsed whole days from November 3, 2026, and any laptop instruction supported by the current notice. Do not add unsupported details."
Source notice A, updated October 28, 2026: "Robotics club meets Tuesday, November 10, 2026, at 4:30 p.m. in Lab 2. Library laptops will be provided. This notice replaces the October 20 notice."
Source notice B, dated October 20, 2026: "Robotics club meets Monday, November 9, 2026, at 4:00 p.m. in Lab 1. Members should bring their own laptops."

Supplied tool result: "Elapsed whole days from 2026-11-03 to 2026-11-10: 7." Apply the same scenario convention: use date-only inputs in the same timezone and calendar context, count midnight-to-midnight transitions, and exclude November 3 as the starting date. The result is 7 transitions, not an inclusive count of the 8 calendar-date labels November 3 through November 10.
Candidate answer: "Robotics club meets Tuesday, November 10, 2026, at 4:30 p.m. in Lab 2, which is 7 days after November 3, 2026. Bring your own laptop."
The candidate contains one detectable factual mistake. Use only the supplied request, notices, tool result, and fictional capability assumptions.

sections.title: Learner variation: complete the evidence check
paragraphs: Write four labeled lines. Line 1, "Governing source:" name notice A or notice B and explain your choice using its exact date or replacement statement. Line 2, "Mistake:" quote or identify the one candidate claim that conflicts with the governing source. Line 3, "Corrected answer:" provide exactly two sentences satisfying the request. Line 4, "Component map:" identify what the model, application, retrieval, tool, and agentic workflow each do in this fictional scenario.

Check your response before using the answer key. The governing source must be chosen from the supplied notices. The correction must not add an event detail that is absent from that source. Preserve the supplied seven-day value using the stated convention: count midnight-to-midnight date transitions, exclude the starting date, and assume date-only inputs in the same timezone and calendar context. November 3 to November 10 is 7 transitions, although inclusive counting would identify 8 calendar-date labels. The component map must not call the model the source of the meeting facts or the date calculation.

Expected result: a complete response chooses the October 28 notice, changes the laptop instruction, preserves the supported meeting details and seven-day count, and assigns each system component a distinct role. If one of those elements is missing, use the specific feedback in the separate answer-key section.

sections.title: Learner variation: separate explained answer key
paragraphs: Governing source: Notice A, updated October 28, 2026. It is later than notice B, dated October 20, 2026, and it explicitly says that it replaces the October 20 notice. Therefore, notice A governs the meeting and laptop details.

Mistake: "Bring your own laptop" conflicts with notice A. The current notice says that library laptops will be provided. This is the only detectable factual mistake in the supplied candidate. The meeting date, time, and room match notice A. The seven-day value matches the supplied tool result and represents 7 midnight-to-midnight transitions from November 3 to November 10, excluding the starting date, for date-only inputs in the same timezone and calendar context. It is not an inclusive count of the 8 calendar-date labels.
Corrected answer: "Robotics club meets Tuesday, November 10, 2026, at 4:30 p.m. in Lab 2, which is 7 days after November 3, 2026. Library laptops will be provided."

Why the correction is justified: the first sentence keeps the date, time, and room from notice A and the count from the tool result. Under the scenario convention, November 3 to November 10 crosses 7 midnight-to-midnight date transitions because the starting date is excluded; counting both included endpoints would instead enumerate 8 calendar-date labels. The second sentence replaces a conflicting instruction with the laptop statement in notice A. It does not claim that members must reserve laptops, arrive early, or take any other action not present in the source.

Component map: the model drafts the reminder; the application connects the interface and components; retrieval locates notices A and B; the date tool supplies 7; and the agentic workflow sequences those permitted operations before pausing for staff approval.
Specific correction feedback if you selected notice B: compare the notice dates and read the final sentence of notice A. The newer notice explicitly replaces the older one.

Specific correction feedback if you changed the date, time, room, or day count: those candidate details already match notice A and the supplied tool result. Correct only the unsupported laptop instruction.
Specific correction feedback if your answer says to bring a laptop: replace that sentence with the current notice's statement that library laptops will be provided.
Specific correction feedback if you added a reservation, arrival, cost, or registration instruction: remove it because neither current notice nor the request supplies that detail.

Specific correction feedback if you called the model the source: notice A is the source of meeting and laptop details, while the tool result is the source of the seven-day count. The model transforms those inputs into prose.

Specific correction feedback if you omitted a component: name all five separately. Model means generation, application means coordination and interface, retrieval means locating notices, tool means the defined date operation, and agentic workflow means selecting and sequencing permitted actions.

sections.title: Use a repeatable evidence-first method
paragraphs: First, restate the requested output and constraints. Exact length, required fields, permitted sources, and forbidden additions make a task checkable. If the request is ambiguous, ask for clarification rather than silently inventing intent.

Second, separate every factual claim in the candidate. Match each claim to a supplied source or an explicit tool result. A sentence can contain several claims, and one wrong detail does not make every other detail wrong.

Third, resolve conflicts using an explicit rule from the request or evidence. In both scenarios, the request says to use the most recent notice, and the newer source says that it replaces the older source. Do not invent a priority rule when none is supplied.

Fourth, correct only what the evidence supports. Preserve supported content, remove unsupported additions, and state unresolved uncertainty when evidence is missing. If no source establishes a required fact, the honest result is that the fact is unsupported, not a guessed value.

Fifth, keep authority with the appropriate person. Drafting a reminder is reversible, but publishing it can affect real people. In these fictional workflows, the system pauses for human approval. In other settings, required review depends on the actual task, permissions, consequences, and available evidence.
sections.callout: Ask two separate questions: What can the system produce, and what evidence lets a person trust this particular output?

activity.title: Correct the supplied library reminder and map the system
instructions: Use only the request, notices, tool result, and fictional capability assumptions in the section "Learner variation: library reminder inputs." No account, code, web search, or invented detail is needed.
Write the four labeled lines required by "Learner variation: complete the evidence check": Governing source, Mistake, Corrected answer, and Component map.
For Governing source, choose notice A or notice B and support the choice with the supplied date or replacement statement.
For Mistake, identify the one candidate statement that conflicts with the governing notice. Do not speculate about why the model generated it.

For Corrected answer, write exactly two sentences containing the supported date, time, room, elapsed-day count, and laptop information. Keep the supplied value of 7 under the scenario convention: for date-only inputs in the same timezone and calendar context, count midnight-to-midnight transitions and exclude the starting date rather than inclusively counting both calendar-date labels.
For Component map, give a distinct role to the model, application, retrieval, date tool, and agentic workflow.
Compare your response with the separate section "Learner variation: separate explained answer key." Apply the specific correction feedback for any mismatch.
evidence: A governing-source choice supported by the October 28, 2026 update date or its explicit replacement statement.
Identification of "Bring your own laptop" as the conflicting candidate claim.

A two-sentence corrected reminder stating Tuesday, November 10, 2026, 4:30 p.m., Lab 2, 7 days after November 3, 2026, and that library laptops will be provided. The 7-day value is treated as 7 midnight-to-midnight transitions that exclude the starting date, not as an inclusive count of 8 calendar-date labels.

A component map that assigns drafting to the model, coordination to the application, notice location to retrieval, date calculation to the tool, and action sequencing plus approval handoff to the agentic workflow.
activity.reflectionPrompt: Which part of the answer came from a source note, which part came from the supplied tool result, and why would calling the model the source blur that evidence boundary?

cues.text: Define model, application, retrieval, tool, and agent before asking learners to classify any behavior.
Show an application boundary containing a model, retrieval component, and tool, followed by an agentic sequence that pauses for human approval.
cues.accessibilityAlternative: Read a static list in this order: application coordinates; retrieval locates notes; tool calculates; model drafts; agentic workflow sequences permitted actions; person reviews.

cues.text: Emphasize that fluent output is not evidence and that an observed mismatch does not reveal its hidden technical cause.

Read the fictional capability assumptions aloud. Clarify that they define the exercise and make no claim about a real product. Explain that the fictional date tool uses date-only inputs in the same timezone and calendar context, counts midnight-to-midnight transitions, and excludes the starting date, so October 5 to October 10 is 5 transitions even though inclusive counting names 6 calendar dates.

Treat the staff notes and supplied tool result as evidence, and treat the candidate answer as a draft to verify. Compare its date, time, room, and elapsed-day claims one at a time, use the newer replacing note for event details, and describe any conflict without guessing why it occurred.
Ask learners to underline the date, time, room, and elapsed-day claims in the candidate before judging it.
Allow one minute for learners to compare each underlined claim with note A and the supplied tool result.

Demonstrate the evidence chain: select the newer replacing note, check each claim, confirm that 5 means five midnight-to-midnight transitions excluding October 5 rather than six inclusively counted date labels, identify Room A as the conflict, and revise it to Room B.
Check that learners can describe the room mismatch without claiming to know why the model produced it.
Assign each observed function to one component and keep the source notes distinct from the model that drafts prose.

Apply the same evidence-first check to the library scenario. Determine which notice governs, compare every meeting and laptop claim with that notice, verify the elapsed-day claim against the supplied tool result, and keep the model's draft separate from the sources that support the facts.

Organize the response into the four required labeled lines. Justify the governing source from the supplied evidence, identify only the conflicting claim, correct the answer without changing supported details or adding new ones, and assign distinct roles to the model, application, retrieval, tool, and agentic workflow.
Have learners complete the four labeled lines using only the supplied library scenario.
Allow four minutes for the source choice, correction, two-sentence answer, and component map.

Reveal the separate answer key and direct each learner to the feedback matching any error in the learner's response. Confirm that the supplied 7-day value uses the same transition-counting convention, excluding November 3 as the starting date rather than counting 8 included calendar-date labels.
Close with the repeatable method: restate constraints, separate claims, match evidence, resolve conflicts, correct narrowly, and preserve human authority.
Collect the four activity lines and check them against the four listed evidence items.
Begin the knowledge check after learners can distinguish all five components and correct a source conflict without inventing a cause.

questions.prompt: Which statement best distinguishes a model from an AI-enabled application?
choices: A model is the entire product, including every interface and database.
A model maps inputs to outputs, while an application can coordinate the model with interfaces, retrieval, tools, policies, and code.
A model is always a search index, while an application is always a calculator.
There is no meaningful distinction between a model and an application.
questions.explanation: The model is a computational component. The surrounding application can add interfaces, retrieval, tools, policies, memory, and deterministic code.

questions.prompt: In the pottery example, what is the source for the pickup room?
choices: The model's confidence
The supplied date-difference tool result
The September 30 staff note
The fact that the candidate has two sentences
questions.explanation: The September 30 note states Room B and explicitly replaces the older note. The model transforms that evidence into prose but is not the source of the room detail.

questions.prompt: What can be concluded from the pottery candidate saying Room A?
choices: The observable room claim conflicts with the governing note.
The model definitely copied its training data.
The application definitely had no retrieval component.
The date tool definitely changed the room.
questions.explanation: The supplied evidence establishes a conflict with note A. It does not reveal the hidden technical cause of the generated text.

questions.prompt: Which action makes the fictional workflow agentic rather than merely a single model response?
choices: Displaying text in a large font
Sequencing retrieval, a tool call, drafting, and a pause for approval
Using a two-sentence prompt
Including a date in a note
questions.explanation: An agent plans and executes actions on a user's behalf. The fictional workflow selects and sequences permitted operations, then stops at its approval boundary.

questions.prompt: Which corrected laptop sentence is supported by the current library notice?
choices: Reserve a laptop online before the meeting.
Bring your own laptop.
Library laptops will be provided.
Arrive thirty minutes early to collect a laptop.
questions.explanation: The October 28 notice explicitly says that library laptops will be provided. The other choices are contradicted by or absent from the governing source.

questions.prompt: What should a reviewer do when a required fact has no support in the supplied evidence?
choices: Guess the most likely value and state it confidently.
Report that the fact is unsupported, request evidence, narrow the task, or stop.
Attribute the missing fact to model training.
Treat fluent wording as sufficient proof.
questions.explanation: A reviewer should make the evidence gap visible rather than inventing support. The task can be clarified, narrowed, handed off, or stopped.
